Question: CREATE TABLE url_cache ( url VARCHAR(767) NOT NULL, content TEXT, PRIMARY KEY (url) ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
What was the problem?: In InnoDB with utf8mb4 each character takes up to 4 bytes so a VARCHAR(767) primary key requires up to 3068 bytes which exceeds the engine's 767-byte key length limit causing table creation to fail.
How would you fix it?: Limit the PRIMARY KEY to a prefix of 191 characters (191 x 4 = 764 bytes) to stay within the InnoDB limit.
Answer: CREATE TABLE url_cache ( url VARCHAR(767) NOT NULL, content TEXT, PRIMARY KEY (url(191)) ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
Comment: utf8mb4 requires a prefix index on string primary keys; always verify byte width against the engine key length limit.

Question: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* TO 'testuser'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'Password1!';
What was the problem?: MySQL 8 removed the IDENTIFIED BY clause from GRANT. Using it causes an error and breaks any database initialization script running on MySQL 8+.
How would you fix it?: Separate user creation and privilege assignment into two statements.
Answer: CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS 'testuser'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'Password1!'; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* TO 'testuser'@'%';
Comment: In MySQL 8+ always use CREATE USER to set the password and GRANT separately.

Question: CREATE DATABASE ace_auth DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8 COLLATE utf8_general_ci; CREATE DATABASE ace_character DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8 COLLATE utf8_general_ci; CREATE DATABASE ace_world DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8 COLLATE utf8_general_ci;
What was the problem?: Running the schema script on an existing installation throws an error instead of a warning causing the entire setup to fail.
How would you fix it?: Add IF NOT EXISTS to each CREATE DATABASE statement so re-running the script on an existing database is safe.
Answer: CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS ace_auth DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8 COLLATE utf8_general_ci; CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS ace_character DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8 COLLATE utf8_general_ci; CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS ace_world DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8 COLLATE utf8_general_ci;
Comment: Always use IF NOT EXISTS in schema creation scripts to make them idempotent and safe to run multiple times.

Question: INSERT INTO letter (module, code, branchcode, name, is_html, title, content, message_transport_type) VALUES ('members','MEMBERSHIP_EXPIRY','','Account expiration','Account expiration','Dear <<borrowers.firstname>>...','email');
What was the problem?: The INSERT provides 7 values for 8 columns. The is_html value is missing causing ERROR 1136: Column count doesn't match value count at row 2.
How would you fix it?: Add the missing is_html value (0) in the correct position between name and title.
Answer: INSERT INTO letter (module, code, branchcode, name, is_html, title, content, message_transport_type) VALUES ('members','MEMBERSHIP_EXPIRY','','Account expiration',0,'Account expiration','Dear <<borrowers.firstname>>...','email');
Comment: Always verify that the number of values in an INSERT matches the number of declared columns exactly.

Question: create index ACT_IDX_MODEL_DEPLOYMENT on ACT_RE_DEPLOYMENT(DEPLOYMENT_ID_);
What was the problem?: The index was created on ACT_RE_DEPLOYMENT instead of ACT_RE_MODEL so it has no effect on the queries that filter on ACT_RE_MODEL.DEPLOYMENT_ID_ causing unnecessary full table scans.
How would you fix it?: Create the index on the correct table.
Comment: Always verify the target table when creating an index; an index on the wrong table silently fails to improve query performance.
